newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet -Telecom merge to bring cash Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Stet -Telecom merge to bring cash Treasury.

text.p: Italy's move to merge state telcommunications holding Stet with state controlled Telecom Italia SpA will increase revenues for the Treasury, the undersecretary to the Prime Minister said.
Undersecretary Enrico Micheli told reporters the concept of the holding company as a box containing other companies was an Italian anomaly.
"(The merger) means helping the privatisation and containing the holding's discount," said Enrico Micheli.
Stet trades at a large discount to the companies it contains.
Micheli added that the operation to merge the companies would take between five to seven months and the sale of Stet, which had been set for March 1997, would be delayed.

He said the transfer of Stet shares to the Treasury from state industrial holding Iri -- which now holds 64 percent of Stet's ordinary share capital -- and the consequent reduction of Iri's debts "needs the support of legislation, of a law."

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, meeting EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert in Brussels on Monday, proposed various hypotheses for reducing Iri debt, which Brussels has been pressing for.
One included transferring Stet shares from Iri to the Treasury, which would also take up some of Iri's debt, although Ciampi said this would require new legislation.
But Micheli told reporters that, in his opinion, the problem of creating a watchdog to regulate the telecommunications sector remained even with the new merger.
The privatisation of Stet has been hampered by a delay in passing legislation to create a regulator, which is a prerequisite for the sale.
